comps: Marks

Face-to-face: 3 pieces x22 (66; each marked fluency & accuracy 7, technical facility 7, communication & interpretation 8) + technical work 14 + two supporting tests 20 (Gr6-8: sight reading 10 + aural/improvisation 10); total 100. Initial: a short technical exercise instead of scales. Pass 60-74, Merit 75-86, Distinction 87-100 (45-59 Below Pass 1). Technical work format F2F: lip flexibility exercise (memory) then scales & arpeggios (memory; examiner picks from items of sets A and B combined, tongued/slurred as requested, scale then arpeggio, f or p; Gr6-8 major = scale+arpeggio, minor = melodic, harmonic, arpeggio; pace quavers) or exercises (prepare 3, one per group; candidate picks first, examiner picks one more; music allowed) or Gr6-8 orchestral/brass band extracts (prepare all 3, play two). Digital technical pathway: 3 pieces x22 (66) + technical work 14 + overall performance 20 (delivery & focus 10, musical awareness 10); technical work is one unit, candidate chooses scales set A or B (memory) or two exercises (different groups) or two extracts; digital Repertoire-only pathway: 4 pieces x25 (8/8/9 components) = 100. UCAS: Gr6 8/10/12, Gr7 12/14/16, Gr8 18/24/30 pts (pass/merit/dist). Scale pace figures are minimum tempi for even quavers. Choosing pieces

Three pieces from the current repertoire list (trinitycollege.com/brass): two accompanied from group A and one unaccompanied from group B (digital Repertoire-only: four pieces, at least two A and one B). Initial-Gr3: one group A piece may be a duet (horn, trumpet, cornet, flugelhorn, euphonium, baritone, trombone only; play upper part, duet partner on a brass instrument, no piano). Own composition allowed instead of a listed piece (accompanied replaces A, unaccompanied replaces B; must be notated, on stave at Gr6-8; durations 0.5-1 min Initial rising to 3.5-5 min Gr8). Observe repeats of 4 bars or fewer; da capo/dal segno observed; cadenzas optional; memory optional with no extra marks; no metronome. Bb trumpet: related instrument allowed for one piece from Gr3. Eb soprano cornet may choose pieces from tenor horn list (and vice versa Gr6-8); bass trombone may swap group B for trombone group B. Any two of: sight reading (30s prep, approx two grades lower; as Initial, 2/4-4/4, 5th range); aural; improvisation (8 bars total (F/G major)); musical knowledge (note values, key/time signature meaning, ledger lines (2), terms and signs). comps: Marks

Face-to-face: 3 pieces x22 (66; each marked fluency & accuracy 7, technical facility 7, communication & interpretation 8) + technical work 14 + two supporting tests 20 (Gr6-8: sight reading 10 + aural/improvisation 10); total 100. Digital technical pathway: 3 pieces x22 (66) + technical work 14 + overall performance 20 (delivery & focus 10, musical awareness 10); technical work is one unit, candidate chooses scales set A or B (memory) or two exercises (different groups) or two extracts; digital Repertoire-only pathway: 4 pieces x25 (8/8/9 components) = 100. Lip flexibility exercise notation is in the syllabus/Trinity brass resources (not reproduced here).
Choosing pieces

Three pieces from the current repertoire list (trinitycollege.com/brass): two accompanied from group A and one unaccompanied from group B (digital Repertoire-only: four pieces, at least two A and one B). Initial-Gr3: one group A piece may be a duet (horn, trumpet, cornet, flugelhorn, euphonium, baritone, trombone only; play upper part, duet partner on a brass instrument, no piano). Own composition allowed instead of a listed piece (accompanied replaces A, unaccompanied replaces B; must be notated, on stave at Gr6-8; durations 0.5-1 min Initial rising to 3.5-5 min Gr8). Observe repeats of 4 bars or fewer; da capo/dal segno observed; cadenzas optional; memory optional with no extra marks; no metronome. Recorded accompaniment allowed up to Gr3 in F2F (live piano from Gr4) and at all digital grades; non-piano accompaniment needs prior approval. Gr4+ (and Gr6-8 tuning) candidate tunes own instrument. Bb trumpet: related instrument allowed for one piece from Gr3. Eb soprano cornet may choose pieces from tenor horn list (and vice versa Gr6-8); bass trombone may swap group B for trombone group B. Euphonium list usable for tuba. Treble/bass clef options for euphonium, baritone, trombone, tuba.
Before you enter
None: no theory or lower-grade prerequisite for any grade.
Digital exams

Digital graded exams (from Dec 2024) are filmed as one continuous take and offer two pathways: Technical work pathway (3 pieces, technical work, overall performance; no sight reading/aural/improvisation/musical knowledge, replaced by overall performance marks) or Repertoire-only pathway (4 pieces). Backing tracks allowed in digital exams at all grades; same repertoire and technical lists as face-to-face.
sections: Scales & technical work

Lip flexibility exercise (Gr8, memory) then EITHER Set A (pace 88-132): Bb major 3 oct f slurred; F# major 2 oct p tongued; C# minor 2 oct mf tongued; whole-tone on Bb 3 oct p tongued; dom 7th in B 2 oct f slurred; dim 7th on Bb 3 oct mf tongued; augmented arpeggio on Db 2 oct p tongued; C major hand-stopped scale 1 oct mf tongued; OR Set B: F# major 2 oct mf tongued; Bb minor 3 oct f slurred; Db major 2 oct mf tongued; chromatic on F# 2 oct mf tongued; dom 7th in Eb 3 oct p tongued; dim 7th on F# 2 oct f slurred; augmented arpeggio on Db 2 oct p slurred; C major hand-stopped 1 oct mf tongued; major = scale+arpeggio, minor = melodic, harmonic, arpeggio; OR two orchestral extracts (Orchester Probespiel: French Horn): Beethoven Sym 9 mvt 3; Brahms Sym 2 mvt 2; Strauss Till Eulenspiegel or Mahler Sym 7 Nachtmusik.
Sight-reading

Sight reading: unseen extract, 30s prep, approx two grades lower than the exam. Parameters: two octaves plus one note, duplets, changing time signatures; transposed at Gr6-8 (C major read for Eb horn).

Two tests (10 marks each): sight reading (mandatory; two octaves plus one note, duplets, changing time signatures) plus either aural or improvisation (16 bars (C#/F minor, 5/4, 7ths/9ths/suspensions)). Sight reading is transposed: key of C major read as horn in Eb (down a tone), examiner plays first note; Gr8 includes simple bass clef. Aural: 12-16 bar harmonised piece, major/minor: time signature, dynamics, articulation, three other characteristics; with copy locate three changes described as pitch or rhythm.

exams.syllabus: RQF Level 4 (EQF 4/5); Ofqual qualification no. 600/0949/4
comps: Entry requirement
None formal: no minimum age, no prior grade or theory qualification required.
Format & marks

Available face-to-face (at Trinity centres, no audience) and digital (one continuous unedited video, max 3GB, uploaded with written programme, any approval letter and one scan per piece; audience allowed). Own-choice programme approval: whole programme only, usually within 15 working days; the syllabus says the approval letter is valid 3 years, while a support article says 2 years (conflict, check the letter). Works on any current Trinity grade, certificate or lower-diploma list cannot be own-choice, and a work approved for one diploma cannot be reused at a higher diploma. comps: Entry requirement
No formal prerequisite. Trinity strongly advises LTCL (or an equivalent Level 6 qualification) in the same instrument or voice first.
Format & marks
Available face-to-face or as a digital (video) exam. Recital 42–48 min performing time (exam slot 50 min). Not marked: the result is Approved or Not Approved.
Programme rules

Programme of at least two works (singing/percussion three), showing a range of moods, styles and tempi; any order. Works complete unless the list specifies movements. Programme may be all list repertoire, list + own-choice, or all own-choice; any own-choice (or single movements of works listed as complete) must be pre-approved as a whole programme via trinitycollege.com/approvals. Accompanied candidates may include unaccompanied works up to 40% of the programme. No viva/discussion component is mentioned in the March 2026 syllabus. FTCL requires full written programme notes of 1,200-1,600 words (context, structure, style, interpretative intent). Equivalent to a postgraduate conservatoire recital.
sections: About the repertoire list

Official FTCL repertoire list for horn, read from the Trinity PDF (25 entries). Programmes must consist of a minimum of two works, performed complete except where single movements are specified. Programmes may use list pieces, own-choice pieces or both, but any own-choice repertoire must be pre-approved. Performance durations: ATCL 32-38 min, LTCL 37-43 min, FTCL 42-48 min. Own-choice music is also allowed within the programme rules above. Check the board's current list before entering; lists are updated online.
General notes

No Grade 8 or Theory of Music prerequisite for any performance diploma (Trinity entry-requirements page and March 2026 syllabus). Current documents: 'Classical Music Performance Diplomas' syllabus, online edition March 2026 (resource id 8556, same for all instruments; Trinity points to trinitycollege.com/performance-diplomas for the current version) and 2026-edition instrument repertoire lists. Digital diplomas (ATCL, LTCL) allow recorded/backing-track accompaniment; face-to-face exams need a live accompanist. Own-choice programme approval: whole programme only, usually within 15 working days; the syllabus says the approval letter is valid 3 years, while a support article says 2 years (conflict, check the letter). Works on any current Trinity grade, certificate or lower-diploma list cannot be own-choice, and a work approved for one diploma cannot be reused at a higher diploma. Up to 30 s allowance for unshortened introductions/tuttis; gaps between movements about 10 s. Short programmes may be penalised.com resource IDs were mis-identified by the fetch tool, but every list used here was confirmed by its heading and by at least two consistent fetches.
General rules (all instruments)

Applies to all instruments. Performance times cover all works including short breaks between movements (about 10 seconds maximum) but not between works; the minimum has no leeway and under-length recitals are referred and penalised, while over-length ones may be curtailed. Programmes show a range of moods, styles and tempi. Use only one instrument type (family members such as flute and piccolo allowed; for flute at most one piece on piccolo or alto flute). Unaccompanied works may make up to 40% of an accompanied programme (one long listed work above 40% is accepted); pieces published with accompaniment may not be played unaccompanied; the candidate provides one accompanist (normally). Repeats: observe da capo and dal segno but do not play exposition or recapitulation repeats, repeats of more than two bars, or repeats within variations (Baroque suite repeats are allowed only if musically justified by ornamentation). Long introductions, endings and tuttis must be shortened (up to 30 seconds allowed). All cadenzas should be played. Memory is not required and earns no marks; metronomes and spoken introductions are not allowed. Music must be from a reliable, unaltered edition and legal copies are needed (copies for the examiner, and originals shown). Stagecraft is marked. A written programme (names, date, composers, full titles with movements and opus numbers, timing per piece and total, in order) is required.
Other components

Programme and planning section requires a written programme with programme notes on every piece totalling 1,200-1,600 words (musical and historical context, structure and form, significant musical elements; sources must be credited and not plagiarised). The balance and order of the programme are also judged. No viva or quick study.
